DONE <- `verus /work/ringbuffer_enqueue.rs` prints `verification results:: 10 verified, 0 errors` with no errors.

The enqueue is implemented in `/work/ringbuffer_enqueue.rs`, and the two postconditions (not-full append and full overwrite) are proven.

**Approach**
- **Not full (`len < cap`):** write `value` at physical index `(head + len) % cap` and increment `len`. The index is computed without overflow as `head - (cap - len)` or `head + len`.
- **Full (`len == cap`):** overwrite the slot at `head`, then advance `head` to `(head + 1) % cap`. `len` stays at `cap`.
- **Helpers** (in the `<helpers>` block): `lemma_mod_shift` (mod distributes over an offset), `lemma_mod_inj` (distinct offsets below `cap` give distinct slots), `lemma_idx` (the branch index equals `(head+len)%cap`), and `lemma_head_next` (the new head equals `(head+1)%cap`).
- **Proofs:** the not-full case uses `assert_seqs_equal!` with the helpers. The full case uses an explicit `assert forall` over indices `0..cap`, split into the last index (which reads the overwritten slot) and the rest (which read old index `i+1`).

**Edits**
- Changes are confined to the `<helpers>`, `<code>` and `<proofs>` blocks (the proofs block is empty). All marker comments are kept.
- The preamble, `use` lines, signature, `requires`/`ensures`, and `fn main` are unchanged.
- No `assume`, `admit`, `unsafe`, `extern`, `external_body`, or other trust attributes are used.
- There are no recursive functions and no `while` or `loop`.
- Scratch files I created are removed; only the two original files remain in `/work`.
